## Purpose and entry points
This repository repackages OpenAI’s signed Linux ChatGPT `.deb` into a community-branded `codex-desktop` distribution. It preserves the upstream Electron payload by default, optionally patches its ASAR for Linux features, and emits native packages, AppImage, and Nix outputs. Primary operator entry points are `Makefile`, `install.sh`, `scripts/bootstrap-wizard.sh`, and the installed launcher template at `launcher/start.sh.template`.

## Upstream acquisition and verified application assembly
The build pipeline resolves the latest official signed APT package, verifies repository/package metadata, extracts its payload, and transactionally replaces the generated application tree only after validation. Shell/Node orchestration and reusable package/upstream logic are concentrated in `scripts/lib/upstream-linux-package.sh`, `scripts/lib/upstream-linux-package.js`, and `scripts/lib/candidate-install.sh`. The generated `codex-app/` is a runtime artifact, not source; all packaging consumes it as the boundary between assembly and distribution.

## Feature selection and ASAR patch framework
Optional features are declarative units under `linux-features/<id>/`, selected locally through the ignored feature configuration. Each can stage files, patch the upstream application, install hooks, and validate compatibility. The common feature contract and selection logic live in `linux-features/compatibility.json`, `scripts/lib/linux-features.js`, and `scripts/lib/linux-features.sh`. Patch execution is centralized in `scripts/patches/engine.js`, `scripts/patches/runner.js`, and `scripts/patches/descriptor.js`; this is the critical integrity boundary because feature-free builds must retain an identical upstream ASAR.

## Native Linux capability services
Several enabled features introduce Rust-backed processes rather than modifying Electron alone. `computer-use-linux/src/main.rs` and `computer-use-linux/src/server.rs` expose desktop-control services, with compositor/window-system adapters in `computer-use-linux/src/windowing/` and accessibility/screenshot/input integration in `computer-use-linux/src/atspi_tree.rs`. Feature-side Node services bridge the patched app/plugin protocol to that native backend via `linux-features/computer-use-linux/native-service.mjs` and `linux-features/computer-use-linux/native-protocol.mjs`.

## Record/replay and companion helpers
The record-and-replay subsystem is a separate Rust runtime that captures events, audio, OCR/browser observations, and turns recordings into reusable skills/MCP-facing artifacts. Its executable/library boundary is `record-replay-linux/src/main.rs` and `record-replay-linux/src/lib.rs`; recording timeline and MCP flow reside in `record-replay-linux/src/recorder.rs` and `record-replay-linux/src/mcp.rs`. Smaller native companions include global dictation (`global-dictation-linux/src/main.rs`) and Linux read-aloud (`read-aloud-linux/src/main.rs`).

## Packaging, launch, and supported runtimes
Distribution-specific scripts package the assembled tree as deb/RPM/pacman/AppImage; common package behavior is in `scripts/lib/package-common.sh`, with format surfaces in `scripts/build-deb.sh`, `scripts/build-rpm.sh`, and `packaging/appimage/AppRun`. The launcher applies Linux environment/runtime policy and starts the retained upstream Electron app through `launcher/start.sh.template`. Nix integration is first-class through `flake.nix`, `nix/linux-features.nix`, and `nix/nixos-module.nix`.

## Update manager and external dependencies
Native packages normally include a Rust user-service updater. `updater/src/main.rs` and `updater/src/app.rs` coordinate CLI/service behavior; `updater/src/upstream.rs` repeats signed upstream discovery, while `updater/src/install_transaction.rs` and `updater/src/rollback.rs` provide staged promotion and recovery. It integrates with systemd user services (`packaging/linux/codex-update-manager.service`) and native package managers. External trust/runtime dependencies include OpenAI’s signed APT repository and payload, GPG verification, Electron/Chromium supplied upstream, Linux desktop APIs/compositors, and optional GoatCounter launch telemetry.
